text:
maya: heads-up — canary euw-h100 cluster showing p99 jump after 03:42 deploy. p50 fine, p99 +45%.
ashok: seeing same in prod-canary metrics. traces show kernel fallback path on a subset of hosts.
maya: rollback? it's blocking rollout.
li: probe on host e-03 shows NIC drops and CPU steal during spike. suspect noisy neighbor on host.
serena: interesting — kernel selector logs show 'fallback_scalar' chosen for 22% of requests when kernel_picker timed out.
maya: stack trace and perf snippet:
```bash
perf stat -e cycles,instructions -p <pid>
# sample from a slow request
cycles: 1.2e9
instructions: 3.6e8
cache-misses: 1.1e6
```
ashok: looks like kernel picker RPCs to placement service timed out (50-200ms) -> picker returns slow path. network RTT to placement service was inflated for hosts on the same hypervisor.
maya: can we hotfix by increasing picker timeout or making default less binary? also maybe pinning to l4 kernel for canary only?
li: temporary mitigation: force-use-best-kernel flag for rollout group A. will gate with config -> quick patch.
serena: but if noisy NIC causes RPC timeouts, forcing best kernel might still incur perf regression if placement answer wrong.
ashok: agreed. better to reduce selector timeout to 60ms + add a cache hit bypass so recent good mappings used.
deploy-bot: deploy started: canary-config-2026-03-18a
oncall-bot: alert created: #inc-9835 high p99 euw-h100
maya: ok ashok+li implement timeout+cache tweak. I'll hold rollout until next canary check in 30m. :thumbsup: 
li: pushing PR: github.com/redwood/infra/pull/5098
ashok: running canary smoke now.
serena: preliminary: p99 down 18% across canary hosts, but 2 hosts still noisy. investigating hardware isolation.
maya: if those 2 hosts keep flapping we'll schedule host drain and remediation.
li: re: bisect — the behavior started after merge 5037 (kernel-picker retry change). scheduling bisect but current mitigation probably enough to unblock rollout.
maya: thanks everyone, keep updates here. :rocket:
